title: Encoder · Raw patch bottleneck MAE
purpose: Discover and develop reusable RPB architecture components and encoder tools that operations and application projects can configure, train and compose.
boundary: Own the family definition, supported configuration, portable initialization/preprocessing/training/export/resume surfaces and their scoped evidence, with unimplemented coverage stated explicitly. Cuwacunu and other applications own substantial application training and final docking. Keep architecture, configuration, recipe and trained instance separate; checkpoint scores do not restrict a family to one benchmark shape. Follow the shared encoder component instructions and preserve frozen source and research records.
summary: Develop reusable RPB encoder components and tools; checkpoints are scoped comparison instances. Native36 remains the historical balanced leader: 8/9 market conditions and four primary transfer comparisons. V30 passed 9/9 market conditions with transfer pending. Preserve those successes and causal-eligibility limits.

goals.title: Preserve the RPB family and evidence
goals.description: Keep the native36 balanced achievement, V30 market success, earlier references and failures traceable under their original protocols.

milestones.title: Preserve RPB versions and original research records
milestones.description: The retained evidence identifies RPB-v24.market-01.alt-01 native36 as the historical balanced leader, with 8/9 market conditions and all four primary frozen TEMPO-5 comparisons. V30 later passed 9/9 market conditions; independent transfer remained pending. Later causal-ancestry limits preserve those historical measurements.
acceptance: The family guide and versioned source are retained under the verified component migration.

evidence.label: Native36 balanced milestone and frozen transfer
Historical RPB leaders and V30 market result
Current research roles and task leaders

goals.title: Expose an explicitly selected RPB instance
goals.description: Bind native layout, fitted preprocessing and checkpoint identity to a declared representation space.

milestones.title: Select and verify an operation-facing RPB contract
milestones.description: Select a version and trained RPB instance for a declared operation, document native outputs and masks, and verify record, fit-artifact and temporal compatibility. Preserve earlier scoped results and comparison limits; no instance becomes a universal default.
acceptance: Bind the exact checkpoint/content identity, architecture/configuration, trained preprocessing, output selector/layout and normalization, plus training/exposure provenance or explicit unknowns. A family/version label alone does not identify an experimental instance.

Provide source/support and availability metadata under foundations-temporal-integrity. End-of-window encodings may use the full available window but must not be labeled prefix-causal without the corresponding dependency and perturbation evidence.

Conformance tests exercise source hashes, native shapes, masks, non-finite data, changed preprocessing and incompatible consumer/index cases. The proposed starter composition is blocked until this bound provider contract and its engineering checks are available.

Retain original research receipts and failures under their original protocols. A probe follows or-05-readouts-probe-protocol; a provider implementation receipt is not evidence that retrieval, risk prediction or dynamics are useful.

goals.title: Expose Hx16 capabilities as a reusable toolset
goals.description: Develop reusable RPB components with supported configuration and portable fresh initialization, TRAIN preprocessing, training, inference, export, resume and validation surfaces through documented CLI/library APIs. Derive dimensions and parameter counts from actual architecture constraints; distinguish implemented capabilities from gaps. Keep family, configuration, recipe and trained-instance identities separate. Cuwacunu and other applications own substantial training and final docking; common provider interfaces do not imply shared coordinates or application quality.

milestones.title: Define the RPB tool surfaces and usage contracts
milestones.description: Map existing version-specific APIs, CLI and adapters plus selected future building blocks into common usage conventions; historical model scores and current commands alone do not establish broad toolset coverage. The component-tool mission and shared encoder instructions govern this surface definition; a checkpoint or application-specific benchmark is an evidence instance.
acceptance: Inventory the agreed loading, encoding, export, validation and workflow surfaces, identifying version ownership, implemented interfaces and remaining gaps without selecting a universal RPB instance or resuming research.

Specify versioned CLI/API inputs and outputs, checkpoint/preprocessing and source identities, native output selection, masks, support/availability, operation-specific compatibility and explicit failure/abstention behavior.

Define bounded examples and completion criteria for common provider records and operation integration, retaining distinct local/contextual/global semantics and actual temporal limits rather than inferring them from dimensions or model names.

Separate family definition, supported geometry/capacity configuration, experimental or training recipe and each trained instance. Inventory portable fresh initialization, TRAIN-only preprocessing fitting, objective/optimizer, training, export and checkpoint/resume APIs or explicit implementation gaps. Derive dimensions/counts and declare actual architectural constraints; a benchmark checkpoint must not impose the only constructible shape.

milestones.title: Expose and verify the agreed RPB building blocks
milestones.description: Deliver the agreed callable RPB surfaces, examples and provider-to-operation integration checks, preserving all original research identities and historical evidence. Coverage must demonstrate the agreed reusable component contract and state configuration/training or provider limitations explicitly.
acceptance: Expose the agreed RPB building blocks through documented Linux CLI and reusable library interfaces in the managed container, using common provider contracts while retaining version-specific model loading, inference and export ownership.

Verify selected standalone tools and a bounded provider-to-operation workflow with native layout, preprocessing, masks, source lineage and temporal meaning; exercise incompatible checkpoints/consumers, malformed inputs and missing-artifact failures or abstentions.

Retain actual engineering receipts and examples with explicit coverage and gaps. Keep checkpoints and restricted data private; research runs, fitting and new utility claims retain separate actual bindings, protocol and permissions.

For the selected trainable family surfaces, verify representative supported alternative geometries, latent widths and capacities through fresh construction, forward execution, a real gradient update, export and checkpoint/resume. Bind preprocessing and recipe identities, retain incompatible-configuration refusals and record missing coverage. These engineering checks establish reusable components, while substantial application training and docking remain application-owned.
